hook: Sana puts {P} in a savings plan that pays {r} a year. How much will she have after {years} years?
define: **Interest** is the price of using money. **Simple interest** is paid only on the money you started with. **Compound interest** is paid on your money and on the interest you already earned.
analogy: Picture two mango trees. The first gives fruit only from its own branches. The second drops seeds, and every seed grows into a new tree that gives fruit too. Compound interest is the second tree.
worked: With simple interest, Sana has {simple} after {years} years. With compound interest she has {comp}. The extra {extra} is interest earned on interest.
predict.q: You save {monthly} every month for {years} years at {sipRate} a year. You put in {put}. What will it be worth?
predict.explain: It is worth about {sip}. Different rates give different results, so a fair range is {sipLo} to {sipHi}. Everything above {put} is interest, and much of it is interest on interest.
early: Two friends save {monthly} a month at {sipRate} a year. Asha starts at {startEarly} and Ravi starts at {startLate}. Both stop at {stopAge}. Asha puts in {putEarly} and ends with {early}. Ravi puts in {putLate} and ends with {late}. Asha ends with about {ratio} times as much money, though she saved only {putRatio} times as much.
tradeoff: Compounding rewards patience. Starting early can matter more than saving extra later. The same effect works against you on a loan, where interest on interest makes the debt grow.
mistake.flat: Some people think interest is always a flat percentage of the money they put in. Most savings plans and loans use compound interest, so the amount grows faster over time.
mistake.late: Some people think starting ten years later is almost the same. It is not. Ravi starts only {gap} years later, but he ends with far less than half of Asha's money.
formula: Simple: A = P × (1 + r × t). Compound, once a year: A = P × (1 + r)^t. Rule of 72: years to double ≈ 72 ÷ rate. At {ratePct}%, money doubles in about {double} years.
check.interest_01.stem: Which kind of interest makes your money grow faster over many years?
check.interest_01.opt.a: Compound interest, because it earns interest on interest
check.interest_01.opt.b: Simple interest, because it is easier to work out
check.interest_01.opt.c: They always give the same amount
check.interest_01.why: Compound interest is paid on your money and on interest you already earned. That extra layer grows bigger every year.
check.interest_02.stem: Ravi lends {P}. He earns simple interest at {r} a year for {years} years. How much interest does he earn?
check.interest_02.why: Simple interest is the amount × the rate × the years. {P} × {r} × {years} gives {answer}. The ₹5,900 option adds the original money back in.
check.interest_03.stem: Money grows at {rate} a year. About how many years does it take to double?
check.interest_03.why: The Rule of 72 says the years to double is about 72 divided by the rate. 72 divided by {ratePct} is {answer} years.
check.interest_04.stem: Two friends save the same amount each month and both stop at 58. One starts at 18 and the other at 28. How does the late starter's final amount compare?
check.interest_04.opt.c: Less than half of the early starter's amount
check.interest_04.opt.d: More, because there are fewer years to wait
check.interest_04.why: Money that starts early has more years to earn interest on interest. Ten extra years of saving gives a final amount more than twice as large.
check.interest_05.stem: {P} grows at {r} a year, with interest added once a year. How much will it be after {years} years?
check.interest_05.why: In year 1 you earn ₹1,000, so you hold ₹11,000. In year 2 you earn 10% of ₹11,000, which is ₹1,100. That gives {answer}, not {simple}.
glossary.interest.def: The price paid for using someone else's money.
glossary.principal.def: The original amount of money you save or borrow.
glossary.simple_interest.def: Interest paid only on the original amount.
glossary.compound_interest.def: Interest paid on the original amount and on earlier interest.
glossary.rate.def: The interest charged or earned, as a percentage per year.
glossary.rule_of_72.def: Divide 72 by the rate to estimate years to double.
